decisionsTitle: The paper confirmation says what it is for, what it does and what the person receives
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-02**, on a registration still waiting for its email confirmation (a club member he wants at the start), after reading the «Ziua cursei» box: «Dacă fac „confirmare pe hârtie” primește mail de declarația și așa?» And, once told: «Pune tooltip și info în back-office pt asta».

### What the caption said, and what it left unsaid

The box's caption (`desk.fastTrackHelp`) read: «Înscrierea e confirmată pe loc, fără email; participantul semnează declarația pe hârtie, iar tu o înregistrezi. Dacă e plin, intră pe lista de așteptare.» It left four facts out, and its «fără email» read as if the person got none:

- **When.** The press is for the race-day desk, with the declaration the participant signed on paper in front of the staff member. The staff member records it on their own name — the declaration (`method = PAPER`, `attested_by_staff_user_id`) and, on a registration still waiting for its address, the address too (`email_confirmed_by_staff_user_id`). Nobody on staff signs for anybody (§67, `AGENTS.md` §15.11).
- **The place.** `confirmByStaff` goes through the allocator under the event lock (§67, §348, §615): a person who is not yet seated joins the waiting list when the event is full or somebody waits, and a full waiting list refuses the press, rolling the whole transaction back.
- **The email.** `acceptDeclarationOnPaper` queues `REGISTRATION_CONFIRMED` (the QR code, the race number, the declaration's copy as after an electronic signature, §95) and the club's copy and notice. No «complete the declaration» email is sent: there is nothing left to sign.
- **What it is not.** It is the desk's verb for a person standing there, not a way to skip the email confirmation before the race. For an address that never got its email, the Administrator's «Retrimite emailul» is the verb.

### The new words

Four catalogue lines (`Admin.desk.paperWhen`, `paperPlace`, `paperEmail`, `paperNot`, each under 200 characters, in both languages, quoting only labels the backoffice shows):

- **The registration's page, «Ziua cursei».** An «i» beside the box's title (`ui/PaperConfirmationTip`, the four lines one under another, the tooltip's newline of §257) and, under the button, a caption of three sentences — when, what the person receives, what it is not. The place's rule (the full line) is in the «i» only: the press itself answers it with the refusal's sentence. The «i» and the caption show only where the button does, on a registration that is not yet confirmed.
- **The confirm dialog** (`registrations.confirmOnPaperBody`, `…BodyMinor`): its words kept, one sentence added — «Apoi pleacă emailul de confirmare.» The dialog's generic line that an email will be sent already followed; this one says which.
- **The desk.** The same «i», once, beside `desk.rowHelp` — the page's always-visible line that says what the row buttons do and already names «Confirmă pe hârtie». Not on each row: twenty rows would be twenty identical «i» in a column the volunteer is scanning for names, and the help line is where the page already answers «ce face butonul ăsta». `DeskRow` is untouched. The volunteer reads the same four lines, and the last says that resending the email is the Administrator's.
- **The walk-in form's help** (`desk.fastTrackHelp`, the same fast track): the false-sounding «fără email» became «fără linkul din email», and it says the confirmation email follows.
- **The guide.** The desk's «Nu și-a semnat declarația» job gains the step about the email the person receives, in both languages.

### What was refused

A new verb, a new email or any bypass: the button, its dialog, the allocator and the audit are what they were, and the rule of `AGENTS.md` §15.11 stands — a staff member records what the participant signed; the press is not a way around the allocator, the declaration or the participant's own signature. Also refused: an «i» on every desk row (noise), and a longer caption (§511: one plain sentence per field, the rest behind the «i»).

**Consequences.** `registrations/ui/PaperConfirmationTip.tsx` (new), the registration's page, the desk page, `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Admin.desk.paper*`, `fastTrackHelp`, `Admin.registrations.confirmOnPaperBody*`, the guide's desk job). Test: `tests/integration/registrations/paper-confirmation-tip.test.ts` (both locales; the tip's four lines in order; the box's «i» and caption; one «i» on the desk however many rows); `tests/unit/i18n/plain-words.test.ts` and `tests/unit/staff/guide-words.test.ts` hold the words. No migration, no dependency, no behaviour change.
changelogLine: - **«Confirmă pe hârtie» says what it is for** — an «i» beside «Ziua cursei» on the registration and once on the desk, a three-sentence caption and a line in the confirm window: at the desk, with the paper the participant signed; the place goes through the waiting list when full; the person then gets the confirmation email with the QR code; and it is not a shortcut around the email confirmation. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a registration the desk's paper confirmation is offered on, when the staff member opens its page or the desk, then the registration page's «Ziua cursei» box carries an «i» beside its title and a caption of three sentences, the desk carries one «i» beside the line that says what the row buttons do (never one per row), the confirm window says the confirmation email follows, and the four lines say, in Romanian and English: that it is for the race-day desk with the declaration the participant signed on paper in front of staff and is recorded on the staff member's name; that the place goes through the allocator (the waiting list when full, a full list refuses); that the person receives the confirmation email with the QR code, the number and the declaration's copy and no declaration-to-sign email; and that it is not a shortcut around the email confirmation before the race. No button, dialog, verb or allocator rule changed (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the paper confirmation says what it is for, what it does and what the person receives
